PCR is a molecular technique used to detect DNA sequences of the Bordetella pertussis bacterium. Unlike culture, PCR doesn't require viable (live) bacteria present in the specimen. pages.text: Bhutan is close to eliminating dog-mediated human rabies Skip to main content WHO/Bhutan Bhutan is close to eliminating dog-mediated human rabies © Credits Bhutan is close to eliminating dog-mediated human rabies 1 September 2026 Highlights Reading time: Rabies used to be a serious public health threat in Bhutan, especially in the southern border districts. Now, the country is on the verge of a major achievement: eliminating dog-mediated human rabies for good. This progress didn't happen overnight. It is the result of strong government leadership, years of sustained surveillance, rapid outbreak response, easy access to rabies vaccines after exposure, mass dog vaccination drives, better dog population management, and strong collaboration between human and animal health sectors. Bhutan has not recorded a single human rabies case since 2023—more than two years running. Having met WHO's requirements, Bhutan put together its official National Dossier on the Elimination of Dog-Mediated Human Rabies and asked WHO to independently validate this achievement in June 2026. From 18–21 August 2026, a team of international experts visited Bhutan to verify Bhutan's claim. They verified surveillance and programme data, carried out field visits, assessed programme implementation efforts, and met with key stakeholders across human and animal health sectors. The team confirmed Bhutan's progress and offered recommendations to help sustain Bhutan's achievements.

Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management and Recreation Act (Act) directs the Department of the Interior’s Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and other federal land management agencies to identify opportunities for public recreation, hunting, and fishing. The Act requires agencies to develop a priority list of federal lands, each at least 640 contiguous acres, that are managed by the BLM and have significantly restricted or no public access for recreational uses. Agencies must identify options to improve access and report biennially to Congress upon completion of the list. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Big Bend Group Sites | Utah View Map In Full Screen Overview Families and large groups will enjoy the three reservable group sites at Big Bend. Group sites A and B are located within the main campground along the Colorado River. Group Site C is located across SR 128 and up a small canyon offering a more secluded location. Outdoor enthusiasts will enjoy hiking, mountain biking, whitewater rafting, rock climbing, and four-wheel drive tours in the surrounding parks and public lands. The town of Moab is approximately 30 minutes away and has dining, shopping, sports rentals, tour companies and museums. Recreation Big Bend Campground is a great base camp for mountain biking, hiking, rafting, rock climbing, taking scenic tours, and exploring the area's backcountry roads. Those looking to relax enjoy sitting under the cottonwoods at the group site or on the small beach nearby. Facilities The Big Bend group areas have fire rings with grates, picnic tables, vault toilets, shade shelters, and trash removal. Sites A and B are near the river.
